statement: Marginal or trivial-filtration event bounds P(A_i|F_{i-1}) <= p do not imply P(intersection_i A_i) <= p^m unless the conditioning controls the preceding events or an appropriate joint structure is proved.
assumptions: Fix 0<p<1 and m>=2. Let B be Bernoulli(p), set A_i={B=1} for all i, and set every F_i to the trivial sigma-field.
source: Independent derivation prompted by worker brief's explicit conditional-product warning; primary polymer source still being recovered.
proof_or_counterexample: For each i, P(A_i|F_{i-1})=p. The intersection equals {B=1}, so its probability is p>p^m. A valid sequential product instead requires each previous intersection to be F_{i-1}-measurable.

statement: The cited arXiv:0810.4221v2 Section 8/12(3) model is the 1+1-dimensional Gaussian zero-temperature point-to-line polymer M_n=max_p sum_{v in p}g_v, with n vertices including the origin. The intake's general-dimension Var(log Z_n) statement is an extension, not the exact statement at that locator.
assumptions: Paths start at (0,0), step right/up, and have unrestricted endpoint; independent N(0,1) vertex weights.

source.quote: Improve the fluctuation exponent in directed polymers.

proof_or_counterexample: Primary PDF defines Gaussian path energies, M as the maximal path sum and Var(M)<=C n/log n. No log Z_n or arbitrary-dimensional theorem is stated at the cited locator.

statement: For the source Gaussian polymer, Var(M_n)=H_n+Var(M_n(r)), where H_n=sum_{j=1}^n 1/j and r is obtained by subtracting the Gaussian mean separately from every reachable time layer. For F_{n,beta}=log sum_p exp(beta sum_{v in p}g_v), Var(F_{n,beta})=beta^2 H_n+Var(F_{n,beta}(r)).
assumptions: n>=1, source path geometry including origin; independent standard Gaussian weights; fixed beta>0 for finite-temperature identity.
proof_or_counterexample: Each path visits one of i+1 vertices at layer i. All layer means are Gaussian-independent of their centered residual vector. The path functional equals the sum of layer means plus its residual functional, and layer-mean variances sum to H_n. For log Z the sum of means is multiplied by beta.

statement: The n=2 source polymer has noise overlap R_2(t)=3/2+arcsin(exp(-t))/pi and Var(M_2)=2-1/pi. Therefore full noise overlap cannot decay to zero as t tends to infinity, even within the exact target model.
assumptions: Independent standard Gaussian weights at origin and the two first-step vertices; Ornstein-Uhlenbeck coupling g_t=exp(-t)g+sqrt(1-exp(-2t))g' for t>=0; unrestricted endpoint.
proof_or_counterexample: The origin contributes one common vertex. The two endpoint choices coincide iff correlated Gaussian differences have matching signs, with probability 1/2+arcsin(exp(-t))/pi by the uniform planar Gaussian angle. For the variance write the endpoint maximum as the independent mean plus half the absolute difference.

statement: In the source model, a uniform bound R_n(n^(-a))<=C n^(1-b) for fixed a,b>0 implies Var(M_n)<=n^(1-a)+C n^(1-b). Conversely a bound Var(M_n)<=C n^(1-delta), delta>0, implies R_n(n^(-delta/2))<=2C n^(1-delta/2).
assumptions: n>=2; R_n uses Ornstein-Uhlenbeck time, not noise standard deviation; same model and constants uniform in n; 0<delta<1 in converse.
source: Independent derivation in ATTEMPT.md; arXiv:0810.4221v2 Lemma 3.1 and Theorem 3.2 supply source overlap identity and monotonicity.
proof_or_counterexample: Var(M_n)=integral exp(-t)R_n(t)dt, 0<=R_n(t)<=n and R_n nonincreasing. Split integral at tau=n^(-a). For converse integrate from zero to t and use 1-exp(-t)>=t/2 for 0<t<=1.
